In 2022, he won mostly just on athleticism, but in 2023, his hand usage — speed, violence and precision — improved dramatically, which was a catalyst for his FBS-leading 16 sacks.
strengths: Really impressive all-around athlete for an edge player. Wrestling background shows up in his core strength and balance. 2023 film showed he was aware of his lack of length and consistently used hand swipes before contact. Hands were significantly quicker in 2023. Like his explosiveness from his three-point stance.
weaknesses: Pops straight up when he's rushing from a two-point stance. Gets happy feet before the snap, at times — leads to false steps. Shorter strides don't cover a ton of ground in pursuit. Will lose the length battle versus NFL offensive tackles.
bottom_line: His overall size (length) could prove to be a limiting factor for his potential in the NFL, but his athletic ability should yield a rotational pass-rush role, at worst, with the potential for an impact role as a top-100 pick.

profile: Though he does not bring much from a measurable standpoint, his five-star athleticism is alive and well. His feet are lightning quick, which allows him to consistently get his foot in the ground to drive his legs when bull rushing. He also is an excellent hand fighter. He makes up for his lack of length by always keeping the hands and arms moving to stay unblocked and eventually get away. He is a relentless pass- rusher but is not as an effective run defender when he can't shoot a gap.
strengths: Quick, explosive steps out of his stance — can really stress OTs’ outside shoulder with speed. Relentless pass rush style. He'll take on as many blockers as needed to get to the QB. Feet are incredibly quick. Hand speed is very quick. He can flash the hands to get the OT to commit, then swipe/rip away.
weaknesses: Likes to use long arm moves right now, but likely will not be effective due to his length at NFL level. Overall size is an issue for trench play — looks to be maxed out at 245 pounds. Explosive player, but shorter strides affect how much ground he can cover.
bottom_line: Thomas is a true low-floor/high-ceiling prospect. He is on the older side, but his natural athletic gifts are still worth taking a chance on to continue to develop as a 3-4 pass-rush specialist.

profile: Trice is a "disruption is production" kind of player. His sack totals over the past two years are low compared to some of his peers, but his name is near the top of the pressures leaderboard. He has a frenetic pass-rush style, which has its pros and cons. On one hand, he's going 100% on every play. On the other, his hands can be erratic and misplaced because of it. He loves the physical parts of trench play, which is good since he'll be one of the bigger edge rushers. Interestingly, most of his snaps are from a stand-up position, but he makes it work. His length is somewhat of an issue, and he won't turn the corner like other edge rushers.
strengths: Loves the physicality part of playing in the trenches. Hands are fast and violent. First step in explosiveness is adequate for the NFL. When he goes all-out speed-to-power, he can really move people. Relentless mentality.
weaknesses: Arm length appears to be an issue. Higher posture leads to some lack of natural leverage, especially from that two-point stance. Arm length concerns show up the most when attempting to tackle. Good amount of success comes from a wider alignment to mitigate the need to get up and around the arc.
bottom_line: This is a powerful edge player who will never shy away from the contact trench play demands. You might have to align him a bit wider to unlock his disruption potential, but he is NFL caliber and should be picked in the top 50.

profile: Tupuola-Fetui is a high-effort player who is competitive to the whistle. He has a good feel and understanding of the two- hand swipe, which allows him to stay unblocked when he can keep his distance. When he allows blockers to get into his chest, it is difficult for him to disengage, even against tight ends. However, he does have a nice inside spin as a counter, though he needs more counters. His anchor ability to hold the edge will need work before he can be called upon in that area. He is also a bit stiff, which is why he is most successful in wider alignments.
strengths: Constantly looking for that two-hand swipe to stay unblocked. Nice inside spin as a counter. Good pursuit speed when he turns it on.
weaknesses: Lacks true power for edge position at the next level. Lack of bend. He aligns wider to mitigate that issue. Too easily moved off the ball by OL or stalled by TEs. Feet can slide out from underneath him when trying to anchor.
bottom_line: Tupuola-Fetui is an experienced, high energy, 3-4 outside linebacker who can make a name for himself as a special teamer, but he must get stronger and improve not allowing blockers to get him locked up to become a rotational player on defense.

profile: Turner, a former five-star recruit, played opposite Will Anderson Jr. during his first season as a starter and held his own. He developed his pass-rush plans from his physical gifts that year. The following season, he added weight and strength to become a well-rounded and even more disruptive player. He continues to use the long arm successfully and can now generate even more movement on his speed-to- power reps. He doesn't have the deepest pass-rush bag, but what he does, he does well. He was more of a stand-up rusher in Alabama’s system and appears to be most comfortable in that stance, though he can also rush with his hand in the dirt.
strengths: Good arm length Good change of direction and acceleration to be a true outside linebacker in a 3-4 scheme who can drop and cover Did not have the strength in his game to get off blocks in 2022 but was a much stronger player in 2023 Really impressive speed, both right off the snap and in pursuit NFL-level combination of explosiveness and bend
weaknesses: Hands are fast, but the efficacy of their placement is inconsistent A little too finesse still. Could attack OTs with more ferocity
bottom_line: Although he can continue to improve as a run defender and a tackler, Turner is a first-round type of edge rusher with high- ceiling pass-rush traits who can contribute in year one with a bright future ahead.

profile: Ugwoegbu played off-ball linebacker at Oklahoma for four years before transferring to Houston and playing primarily edge rusher. Whether it's due to experience or total potential, he is better suited as an off-ball player. He has good instincts and downhill pursuit, and he can hit ball carriers with a good pop. As an edge rusher, he is stiff around the arc, lacks pass- rush timing and finesse, and he would need to add more weight for his style of trench play.
strengths: Powerful club move. Extensive experience at every linebacker spot. High-effort player. Good hit power. When playing off the ball, he recognizes where things are going and how to cut them off.
weaknesses: Stiffness up the arc causes Houston to use him in wide-nine technique. Strong for his weight but lacks strength against NFL edge rushers. Pass-rush flow isn't clean. Needs to expand pass-rush repertoire beyond just strength-based moves.
bottom_line: As an edge rusher, Ugwoegbu has a long climb to make a team in the NFL, currently lacking pass rush moves and nuance for that position. However, as an off-ball LB (where he played primarily before 2023), he could be a depth roster special teammer.

profile: Verse is a devastatingly powerful edge player who brings the gym to the field on all three downs. After his 2020 season at Albany was canceled due to COVID-19, Verse and his father built a home gym and he put on 40 pounds in one year. He came back and was an FCS All-American. He transferred to Florida State the following season and displayed overwhelming strength against LSU in just his second game in the FBS. His speed-to-power is consistently effective. His hands are powerful and violent, and his swipes look like they hurt. His best work comes from the power he generates as a three-point defensive end.
strengths: Very powerful player. Speed-to-power move can be devastating Violent hands First-step explosiveness is NFL-caliber Smart with his swim move. He can go to it quickly and instinctively to counter the momentum and direction of a pulling blocker
weaknesses: Significantly less power (leverage) when rushing from a two- point stance, though he is familiar with it Lateral flexibility shows some stiffness. Limits how well he can get across the face or shoot inside
bottom_line: Verse doesn't have the longest arms, and that shows up in some pass-rush counters and in tackling, but he brings his hard hat and lunch pail to every snap, wins with strength regularly and is built like a first-rounder.

profile: Watts is at his best when he can use his length with a long arm and push-pull moves. He also has decent first-step explosiveness for a player of his size. He is light in the lower half, which causes a balance issue and when trying to anchor. His height also causes pad-level issues, as he is consistently playing high and losing leverage. His hand placement could use more refinement, and his pass-rush plan needs to be developed further to maximize his size. His flexibility is also lacking, as it is tough for him to bend, corner or change direction (very low agility scores).
strengths: His length is a huge plus on the edge. Above-average straight-line explosiveness, especially for his size. When he can extend his arms with his hands inside, he can really get offensive linemen on their heels.
weaknesses: Plays with a high pad level, which is unfortunately natural for a player his size. Not very flexible — tough for him to really turn the corner or change direction. Light in the pants to anchor and balance against contact. Hand placement could be more consistent for increased efficiency.
bottom_line: Watts has alluring potential as a 4-3 defensive end with his frame, but he must improve his flexibility, hand placement consistency and his balance/lower body strength before a team can see a return on investment due to his measurables.

profile: As a former all-state quarterback in high school, Barrett has a natural feel for the game. Though overall anticipation could be better, his feel for where blockers are going to be is smooth. His downhill speed is adequate, but that mainly comes from good burst — his long speed for the NFL level is an issue. As a blitzer, he brings a pop at contact with a high motor to get to the quarterback. His biggest detractor is his overall size. Though he understands run fits, he is too easily blocked by guards.
strengths: Very natural football player. he has a great feel for the game, where the ball is going and how to make an impact. Adequate speed to close on the ball or get to space. Good A-gap blitzer. He has the speed-to-power to hit/get past blocking RBs.
weaknesses: Size is a concern for regular linebacker responsibilities at the NFL level. Overpowered by pulling guards. Understands run fits, but his size limits his effectiveness.
bottom_line: Barrett is a natural football player, but he's tough to find a home for in the NFL, as he's too small for linebacker but not athletic enough to play safety. He projects as a potential special teams ace with some defensive responsibilities in dime situations.

profile: Bertrand is an experienced, smart linebacker prospect and an excellent pre-snap anticipator and communicator. He is rarely fooled by the window dressing of play action and pre-snap motion, often cutting off those plays. At 6-foot-1 and 235 pounds, he is on the smaller side. His lack of length is an issue when wrapping up and when getting off blocks. However, he is fundamentally sound in run defense. He is also a smart coverage player but is not as comfortable with shuffling and retreating as he is with keeping things in front of him. Most glaring is that he did not record an interception or a forced fumble in his college career.
strengths: Excellent at pre-snap recognition and communication. Vocal leader Good fundamentals in run defense. Square shoulders at the line, good eyes to find the ball carrier
weaknesses: Lack of length shows when trying to get off blocks Lack of weight is evident on blocks/tackles Average to below-average athlete for NFL standards
bottom_line: Bertrand is a tough, smart and competitive prospect, albeit undersized, who projects as a rotational/backup inside linebacker for 4-3 or 3-4 schemes.

profile: Chambers' running back background and skillset show up in his short area quickness, body control and change-of- direction ability. This allows him to sift through clutter as well as move well in zone coverage. His lack of size is concerning for the position. He understands where to fit the run, but he is easily handled by offensive linemen and sometimes tight ends. His short arms also make it difficult for him to stack and shed. His long speed appears to be average for NFL linebackers, but shorter strides might make that below average. His effort and willingness to be physical despite his lack of measurables is a calling card.
strengths: Good short area quickness and change of direction, which comes from his running back background. Plays with high effort and aggression. Has the upper body strength to stack and shed blocks (though it takes him a bit to do it). Conscious and consistent run fits. Good recognition speed and even some nice anticipation from him.
weaknesses: Willing to take on offensive linemen but lacks the true power to hold up. Lacks the length/weight to shed blocks quickly and cleanly. Pursuit speed feels average at best for the NFL level.
bottom_line: Chambers plays the position with aggression and decisiveness to be an inside linebacker for 3-4 fronts, but he may just simply lack the overall size required to be a starter at the NFL level.

profile: Colson grew up playing soccer in Haiti and began playing football when he moved to the U.S. He committed to Michigan and started 36 of his 41 games played in just three seasons. He is a strong and reliable run defender who has good discipline at the LOS. His feel for coverage is also above average. He has good pre-snap communication and recognition and does not run himself out of plays with play action or pre-snap motion. His straight-line speed is decent, but his change-of-direction ability is tight (slower to flip the hip). Though he is good at sifting through chaos in run defense, he has some difficulties getting off blocks.
strengths: Willing to be physical to take on blocks Good feel for hook/curl and Tampa drop-zone responsibilities Keeps his shoulders square and sifts through chaos in run defense Doesn't run himself out of position versus play action and pre-snap motion Good pre-snap recognition/communication
weaknesses: Good, not great, athlete A bit tight to change direction. Hips are tight Decent at getting off blocks, but can still struggle
bottom_line: Colson's background and journey to this point are inspiring. He has the size and football IQ to play in the NFL. He is a good but not great athlete, which will likely make him a Day 2 pick as a rotational 4-3 linebacker with starting potential.

profile: Cooper brings a lot of athleticism to linebacker. He possesses top-tier change of direction, burst and pursuit speed. His best work comes when he keeps things in front of him, flying in for tackles at the line of scrimmage or the sidelines. Cooper's issues come from reacting more than anticipating. He is manipulated off his spot too often against play action and pre-snap motion. He also tends to overpursue tackles, though he was more consistent in 2023. He earned a high coverage grade in 2023, but that was more from defending shallow zones, running backs out of the backfield and QB scrambles than it was from deeper zone assignments.
strengths: Downhill player who is willing to take on blocks at the LOS Top-tier athlete in change of direction, burst and long speed Effective blitzer
weaknesses: Can be manipulated by pre-snap motion/play action Out of control sometimes. Takes a step too far in one direction and overcommits Reacts more than he anticipates
bottom_line: Cooper has the length and the athleticism to be a starting- caliber linebacker in the NFL in a downhill role. His lack of anticipation and instincts for deeper coverage work will likely keep him from being picked in the first round.

profile: Eichenberg was a two-time captain and a three-year starter at Ohio State. He is a throwback type of linebacker who loves to hit and defend the run near the line of scrimmage. He was superb in that role in 2022, earning an elite PFF run-defense grade. He is slippery between the tackles, quickly sifting through offensive linemen to get to ball carriers. He is a decent athlete when it comes to straight-line speed, but he can get into trouble when asked to flip his hips or change direction. It will be hard to rely on him consistently in spot zones. However, carrying tight ends up the seam or running backs up the sideline is in his wheelhouse.
strengths: Excellent eyes in run defense. Knows where the ball is and how to get to it Slippery between the tackles Good hit power
weaknesses: Long speed will be average at best Change of direction is below average for an NFL linebacker. Will impact coverage ability
bottom_line: Eichenberg is a strong-side linebacker who can find work in early down roles as a Mike/Sam, specifically in a 4-3 defense. However, you won't want him operating in space in sub- package situations in coverage on late downs too often due to a lack of lateral mobility.

profile: Ford was a two-year starter at Texas with 29 starts in total and two first-team All-Big 12 honors. He has played a ton of snaps over the last two seasons and brings leadership to the center of the defense. As an athlete, he is adequate for the NFL even when it comes to running downhill, but he is below average when moving laterally and when shuffling in coverage. To make up for this, he will need to anticipate more consistently at the next level. He has a decent feel for coverage but lacks true recovery athleticism if he gets out of position. As a tacker, he is strong to the ball and possesses decent hit power when making contact.
strengths: Good downhill burst. Good hit power when tackling. Constant pre-snap communicator.
weaknesses: Straight line burst is good but displays stiffness when turning a corner. Can get fooled by play-action. His anticipation needs to improve. Doesn't feel lost in coverage, but if he's a step late, he doesn’t have true recovery athleticism.
bottom_line: Ford projects as a high-energy depth linebacker as a MIKE who could be a consistent contributor on special teams.

profile: His scouting report starts with his speed. He has very good short-area burst and long speed to meet ball carriers at the sideline. He has long arms, which aid him in wrapping up ball carriers. As a blitzer, his lateral movements are quick and explosive. He is a bit light and would do best more as a Will linebacker in space. His coverage in the box is good, but his slot coverage was inconsistent. His biggest area of concern is his anticipation. After three years as a starter, you would like to see him anticipate more than he does now, often reacting to where the ball is going after it moves.
strengths: Above average speed to get to the sideline and cut off ball carriers before they get upfield. Good short-area quickness to avoid blockers and continue moving forward. Useful long arms to wrap up as a tackler.
weaknesses: Play anticipation could improve, as he is slower to break, at times, when reacting to the ball. Lighter in weight and in the lower half, which makes it difficult to hold a gap when defending the run.
bottom_line: Gray is an adequate athlete for Will linebacker responsibilities, but his play recognition must improve to become a starter at the NFL level.

profile: Hopper is a roaming middle linebacker who plays with ideal play speed. He has good explosiveness and natural athleticism. However, his lack of arm length and overall weight will raise the question as to whether he can take on blocks consistently at the next level. He has good a rip move when trying to get by blockers in pass-rush situations. In coverage, he moves well enough to have some responsibility there, but he is too overaggressive, which can lead to bigger throwing windows against him.
strengths: Really nice first step explosiveness. Actually has a nice rip move when coming around the edge as a blitzer. Good movement skills to spot drop in coverage. Play speed is ideal — flies in for tackles.
weaknesses: Lacks both length and mass to be effective taking on and getting off blocks. Need to play more controlled in coverage — he always wants to play fast, but it can hinder him in coverage.
bottom_line: Overall, Hopper is a nice athlete who has potential in both coverage and pass rush despite less impressive measurables. His play speed is a pro and a con for him. If he can be more appropriate with when to turn on the jets and when to be patient, he could be a contributing backer and special teams standout.

profile: Jacobs is an elite athlete for the linebacker position. He has showcased good downhill speed and sideline-to-sideline ability. He can run stride for stride with tight ends getting vertical and with backs running wheel routes out of the backfield. Jacobs' issues seem to come between the tackles. He does not shy away from taking on blocks, but he isn't consistently winning when doing so, even against tight ends. When he misses tackles, it appears to be an arm length and lack of overall strength issue.
strengths: Very explosive downhill athlete. Good body control to change direction and accelerate. Hands are fast when disengaging from blocks. Has the athleticism to be a good coverage defender.
weaknesses: Can get moved off his spot too easily against tight ends. Fast but not overly effective as a pass-rusher. When he misses tackles, it feels like an arm length (25th percentile) and strength issue.
bottom_line: Jacobs is a good athlete with starting potential movement skills, but he must get stronger and continue to improve his coverage instincts to shorten throwing windows.

profile: Liufau is a powerful linebacker at 238 pounds. His first step and speed-to-power ability are imposing, especially as a blitzer. When defending screen and swing passes out of the backfield, he can fly to the ball with a lot of power at contact. That power also shows up when he takes on or sheds blocks. His long speed is likely just average for the position, despite above-average acceleration. He is more comfortable in a downhill role than when retreating in coverage. He has the movement skills to play in coverage, but his instincts and lack of recognition can get him picked on a bit there.
strengths: Nasty when coming downhill Great power at contact despite being just 238 pounds Nice change-of-direction ability/explosiveness Will never shy away from taking on blocks Quick to push/pull blockers in his way
weaknesses: A little slow to recognize where the ball is going Average long speed
bottom_line: Liufau is a powerful downhill linebacker who attacks ball carriers and blockers with bad intentions. His instincts and feel for spot zone coverage still need work if he is to be relied upon consistently. He is projected as a contributing inside linebacker for either a 4-3 or 3-4 defense.

profile: Muasau loves to be physical and does not shy away from doing the dirty work of playing linebacker. His lower size profile makes him quick and explosive, but that lack of weight really shows up when taking on and shedding blocks. He can also be late to recognize where the ball is going.
strengths: Embraces and welcomes the physical requirements of the position. Comfortable and confident in clutter and chaos. Takes pride in doing the dirty work to contain the run and set the edge. Will bulldoze running backs in pass protection.
weaknesses: Can be late to recognize where ball carriers are going. Can get overpowered by most offensive linemen due to lower weight (even with momentum). Plays a style that requires more weight.
bottom_line: Muasau plays a style of linebacker every defensive coach will love, but he needs to add more strength and must anticipate with more regularity to make up for outlier measurables to be more than a special teamer.

profile: Trotter has an incredibly high football IQ, which allowed him to become a starting LB at Clemson as a true sophomore in 2022. He is a fundamentally sound run defender who stays disciplined in his gaps and square to the ball carrier. In coverage, he has good eyes and instincts, which allows him to cover multiple receivers who pass through his area and jump passes. Unfortunately, his measurables are not usually conducive to success in the NFL. His smaller arms make it tougher to wrap up against better ball carriers. His weight means that offensive linemen can move him in run blocking. His pursuit speed will also likely be below average.
strengths: Good instincts/feel in zone coverage Understands the manipulation tactics of play action and pre-snap motion Good patience/eyes for gap shooting Willing to be physical at all times Fundamentally sound run defender
weaknesses: Size deficiencies show up often Long speed looks below average Shorter arm length limits ability to wrap up against better RBs
bottom_line: Trotter is an incredibly smart linebacker who consistently puts himself in the right positions. However, his lack of length, size and explosiveness limit his starting, and even rotational, potential on the NFL stage.

profile: Just a two-star linebacker recruit, Ulofoshio joined Washington as a walk-on. He eventually became a starter and battled through a torn biceps and a torn ACL in the 2021 and 2022 seasons. His perseverance paid off, as he started all 15 games for a Huskies team that made a national championship run in 2023. Ulofoshio's experience allows him to recognize things quickly, especially in coverage. He is still fooled by play action and pre-snap motion. His low recruiting ranking stems from his limited athleticism. When he keeps things in front of him, he can make plays as a tackler. Still, he lacks both straight-line and change-of-direction abilities.
strengths: Significant experience has led to good coverage recognition
weaknesses: Below-average straight-line athlete Slow to react to who has the ball against RPOs, play action and even straight run plays Does not always take the best paths to the ball Can look wild due to lack of change-of-direction control Lack of strength/length makes it tougher for him to get off blocks
bottom_line: Ulofoshio’s journey of hard work and perseverance will have NFL teams enamored. However, his below-average athletic ability limits his ceiling as a likely Day 3 depth linebacker.

profile: At the combine, he confirmed that track explosiveness with 80th and 90th percentile scores in the 40-yard dash, vertical and broad jump. That athleticism shows up on tape, especially when triggering downhill. He can cut ball carriers off quickly, and that leg power brings hitting power when he arrives. He can be a good option for QB spy assignments. While he is an adequate athlete, he still needs to be more consistent in play recognition after the snap. He can often make up for it with his speed at the college level, but that won't be as easy in the NFL.
strengths: Athleticism pops immediately — explosive player. Strong, powerful legs lead to good hit power. Can be a QB spy option against mobile QBs.
weaknesses: Struggles to get off blocks more than he should. Will take aggressive pursuit angles to the ball, which presents a big risk and a big reward. Good burst for pressure off the edge, but he is a bit stiff to turn the corner.
bottom_line: Wallace is a top-tier athlete for the position, but he must improve his anticipation and recognition in order to truly be a difference maker with his physical gifts.

profile: Watson is quite strong, and pairing that with his massive wingspan makes a great tackler and gives him an advantage when taking on blockers. Unfortunately, he doesn't have leverage nearly enough and often takes contact with a high pad level. He is strong downhill, as evidenced by his 25 tackles for loss over the last two years, but is limited to a straight-line athlete. If you ask him to flip his hips or quickly move laterally, he struggles, especially in coverage.
strengths: Long arms (93rd percentile) are an asset when pass rushing and tackling. Strong football player — when he gets his hands on you, he’s bringing you to the ground. Patience is a plus — he won't overrun a gap or a ball carrier.
weaknesses: Lacks the flexibility to stay fluid when changing direction. Too upright when taking on blocks — needs that leverage for better pop. Lack of hip turn quickness limits how effective he can be in coverage. He has the strength and the arm length to stack blockers but doesn't always get off with haste.
bottom_line: Watson is a classic between-the-tackles kind of linebacker who wins with strength and length, but his athletic limitations will likely limit him to early-down work and special teams duties.

profile: Wilson will be one of the older prospects in the 2024 NFL Draft class. He missed time due to injuries at N.C. State, but when on the field, he proved to be one of the best defenders in college football. His 6-foot-4 frame gives him plus pass- rush ability up the middle and around the edge. Despite his knee injuries, he is very fluid for his size, both in coverage and as a pass rusher. That allows him to match and mirror tight ends and running backs, as well as cover a lot of ground in spot-dropping assignments. He can recognize where the flow/ball is going and has the pursuit speed to be impactful. He also has great ball skills for a linebacker.
strengths: Good length to handle blockers and get off blocks Quick trigger downhill Fluid athlete for his size Covers a lot of ground in coverage when shuffling Above-average pursuit speed Good pop at contact despite being listed between 230-235 lbs
weaknesses: Extensive injury history Slender frame and lack of weight show up at times against bigger players
bottom_line: Wilson has the length, movement ability, IQ and tape of a first- round linebacker. What will likely keep him from being drafted on Day 1 is his injury history and age. If healthy, he can be a starting inside linebacker in any defense.

profile: Abrams-Draine started his career at Missouri as a receiver. The three-star recruit even played quarterback in high school as a senior. He moved to defensive back as a sophomore at Missouri and started on the outside in each of the past two seasons. He has a ton of ball production — seven interceptions and 34 forced incompletions — since 2021. Abrams-Draine is a good overall athlete with adequate long speed and recovery speed, fluid hips and an explosive first few steps out of a change in direction. His weight is on the lower side, which is why you won't see him in press coverage much. But he does great work in off-coverage from zone.
strengths: Demonstrates a good feel for off-zone coverage Excels at reading quarterbacks' eyes Has a lot of range in zone coverage, even if he has to flip and turn in the other direction to make a play Shows an impressive ability to flip his hips and get on his horse
weaknesses: Hips don't flip as quickly and as smoothly as you'd want for a slot defender Does not have the nuances of the position mastered yet. Mistimes punches in press and gets fooled by receivers’ shoulders and fakes Didn’t miss many tackles, but when he did, it was due to a lack of strength
bottom_line: Abrams-Draine has a lower weight percentile and is still learning the nuances and anticipation required to play the position at a high level, but he is a fluid athlete with a knack for making plays on the ball. He projects as a CB3 with CB2 potential in a zone- based defense, and he brings special teams experience.

profile: Arnold played mostly outside cornerback for Alabama over the past two seasons but gained some experience in the slot in 2023. He has great long speed, recovery speed, acceleration and agility. He also brings impressive ball skills with good on-ball production. With just one year as a full-time starter, he is a bit erratic in his style and had some missteps and whiffs on punches in press that got him turned around or off-balance. When he's aligned and in phase, he has the talent to shut down all kinds of receivers. Though green on total snaps, he does show a good understanding of post- snap adjustments and man-match principles.
strengths: Top-tier athlete for the position. Recovery speed and long speed will allow him to keep up with NFL receivers Elite stop-and-start ability Baseline understanding of man-match principles Not afraid to stick his nose in run defense
weaknesses: Too comfortable with getting turned around. Knows he's athletic enough to do it Feels too out of control. Some missteps and whiffs on punches in press got him turned around or off-balance A bit too grabby on deep passes Is fooled by footwork too often Leverage is inconsistent.
bottom_line: Arnold isn't the most polished cornerback in this class, but his high-percentile athletic abilities give him as high of a ceiling as any cornerback in man or zone systems.

profile: Brownlee evolved into an NFL-level cornerback in 2023. He likes to be physical and shows that in coverage and run defense. He brings a powerful punch at contact when getting his hands up to disrupt routes and makes things tough for receivers at the catch point. His short-area movement skills are good, from his hip fluidity to his first-step explosiveness. He frequently got his hands on passes due to playing close coverage, but his ball skills don't stand out. He is not as comfortable in off-coverage but could improve there. Brownlee’s biggest issue is his recovery speed, as he lacks the top gear to make up the separation.
strengths: Loves to be physical, especially in press and run defense. Impressive power at the punch when getting hands up in press. Good short-area movement skills. Hips flip quickly and first step is explosive. Will make a receiver really work for it at the catch point.
weaknesses: Long speed/recovery speed could get him in trouble against faster vertical wideouts. Not as comfortable/aggressive with calculating spacing in off- coverage. Looks less comfortable from the slot, even in press (could be a lack of experience).
bottom_line: Brownlee is a competitive player whom press teams will covet, but his middling long speed is a concern when defending vertical routes against NFL athletes.

profile: Bullard is a fiery competitor in the secondary who brings a mentality every NFL team will gravitate toward. He was a starter in the slot in 2022 and at safety in 2023. His best work came from the slot, where he played confidently in press coverage and showed off his willingness and effectiveness in run support. He did not look as comfortable at safety with so much space, and he took overaggressive angles when coming downhill. His in-your-face play style was much more aligned with slot responsibilities.
strengths: Experienced and successful slot defender Fearless tackler for his size Fiery competitor who does not back down from any assignment
weaknesses: Recovery speed is good but not elite Overaggressive pursuit angles cause him to be out of control at times Much more comfortable playing in the slot than coming from depth
bottom_line: Bullard is a versatile secondary player with a fearless mentality. Though he isn't an elite athlete, his competitiveness, quickness and tackling ability project him to a starting role as a nickel defender.

profile: Carson played more than 2,000 defensive snaps over four years at Wake Forest. His calling card is physicality. Though not overly imposing in height or weight, he likes to get his hands on receivers at the top of the route and when they try to get vertical on him. His best athletic trait is his downhill click-and-close ability. His feet and hips are fast and fluid. However, he may also play a lot of off-coverage because his long speed and recovery speed are average to below average. He recorded strong forced incompletion rates but made just one interception in two seasons as a starter. Carson is an impactful run defender, too.
strengths: Displays quick click-and-close ability downhill Very willing tackler Hips can flip fluidly and quickly Likes to keep it physical through the route Plays above his weight class in run defense
weaknesses: Lack of weight/strength shows up when tackling Needs to get hands on receivers to keep up with them vertically
bottom_line: Carson lacks the long speed/recovery speed to play island coverage. He can be a CB2/3 as an off-coverage defender in a zone-heavy scheme, bringing good downhill closing speed and reliable tackling.

profile: DeJean played mostly outside cornerback for Iowa over the past two years. At 6-foot-1 and 205 pounds, he checks the size boxes for the position and brings top-tier natural athleticism. His footwork is quick and controlled, his backpedal and shuffling are smooth, his stop-and-start speed is good for his size and his ball skills are elite. Wrap all that with a bow of high football IQ and instincts. He doesn't have much experience in press coverage but can succeed in that role. DeJean is likely the best run-defending cornerback in the class. There aren't many holes, if any, in his game.
strengths: Great size for a cornerback. Stout in run defense Quick, controlled footwork in his backpedal allows him to veer and break exactly how he needs to Good instincts and football IQ. Communicates and observes the whole field pre- and post-snap Impressive ability to flip his hips and accelerate for his size Has the natural athletic ability to play press Ample special teams experience as a gunner and returner
weaknesses: Only 199 snaps in press (less than 25% over past two years) Change of direction/acceleration when he's fully flipping his hips can be slow because of his size
bottom_line: The talk of DeJean playing outside cornerback or safety or slot cornerback at the next level is not due to lack of a home position; it's because he could truly be an impact player anywhere. His footwork, ball skills and explosive athleticism make him an impactful outside cornerback — one with All-Pro potential.

profile: Dixon was a starter since his second season at South Carolina. He transferred in 2021 to Penn State and was a consistent player, mostly as a wide cornerback but also in the slot. He is a tough evaluation because his athletic traits indicate he would have more success in the slot, boasting quick, controlled and balanced footwork with good stop-start ability and pass-rush quickness. But he lacks strength. He won't be able to hold the edge or shed blocks, even with a full head of steam. That lack of strength is also a concern if projecting him to play on the outside. It makes more sense for him to be matched up against smaller receivers.
strengths: Gained slot experience in 2022 when Joey Porter Jr. and Kalen King were on the outside Body control and stop-and-start ability stand out. Possesses excellent footwork. A very balanced athlete Calm cornerback in trail technique. Doesn't panic and immediately hit full speed recklessly Savvy with his punches in press and at the contact point of routes when in off-coverage. Not imposing, but annoying for WRs
weaknesses: Doesn't back down from matching up against tight ends but is overpowered by them fairly easily Quicker than he is fast. Can get taken advantage of when in press and receivers are running vertically Lacks strength in his finishing ability at the catch point and in run defense 30% missed tackle rate against the run
bottom_line: Dixon might be a rotational matchup specialist against smaller receivers in the NFL. He is fiery in his approach to the position and possesses adequate agility skills for the NFL level. If he can become a more reliable tackler, he certainly has the coverage skills to see the field in some capacity.

profile: Green loves to get up on the line of scrimmage and have only one thing to worry about: not letting the guy in front of him make a catch. He does that well with patient footwork and well-timed hand strikes when receivers get into their routes. He is rarely fooled to get out of control or show false steps. He is not as comfortable in off-coverage. In run defense, he is a willing tackler and conscious of setting the edge, but his lower weight impacts his effectiveness. Though he recorded just two interceptions in two years, he forced 17 incompletions in 2023. His burst and agility are above average, but his long speed is just average for the NFL.
strengths: Lives for press-man coverage. A true "don't let him catch it“ cornerback. Quick but patient footwork to mirror releases. Nice control of his speed. Can chop the feet and then immediately accelerate. Good balance and timing with his hand strikes off the line. Calm demeanor about him. Rarely shows panic steps or false moves.
weaknesses: Can be a bit grabby at the break of routes. Not uncommon for man-coverage cornerbacks. Not a shy tackler, but his lower weight leads to inconsistencies. Not as comfortable or confident to make plays on the ball when in off-coverage. Top-gear speed is just average for the NFL.
bottom_line: Green is a calm and confident man-coverage cornerback with CB2 potential for a team that likes to play in press.

profile: Hadden has been on a winding college football journey, starting as a zero-star recruit who had to go to community college. However, he showed resilience when roadblocks came up, which helped him earn a shot at the NFL. His size- speed combination is alluring. When in control, he is agile, smooth, sticky and can run with vertical receivers in man coverage. He is confident in press but can also be confident in zone, always trying to manipulate space to bait a throw he can jump. His technique is still a major work in progress in press coverage, with his footwork and when tackling, but all areas did improve from 2022 to 2023.
strengths: Ideal size-speed combination for the NFL level. Smoothly flips his hips for his size. Always looks to bait quarterbacks into a throw when in off coverage – a dangerous game, but he's confident in it.
weaknesses: Frenetic footwork in press coverage in 2022 — more controlled in 2023. Incorrect hand technique in press causes him to allow separation against vertical routes. Dangerous tackling technique in 2022 — constantly dipped his head to show the crown of the helmet before launching. 2023 showed tackling technique still needs a lot of work.
bottom_line: If you draft by the motto of "just draft talented dudes and let the coaches do the rest," Hadden will be a top 100 player. However, the honest assessment is he still has a ways to go in run defense and press coverage techniques before he can showcase his physical gifts in the NFL.

profile: Harden is smaller, which will be an issue if he is to stay at outside corner in the NFL. However, he is feisty and a willing run defender. He likes to get his hands on receivers and make them work for their route. His long speed is a concern against vertical receivers, but his short-area quickness makes up for it on in-breaking routes and underneath throws.
strengths: Physical and competitive mentality is evident very quickly when watching his tape. He will not only come up and tackle but will give ball carriers some pop. Controlled, quick athlete.
weaknesses: Lacks the length to really compete with NFL-size receivers. Long speed is a concern for vertical receivers at the next level.
bottom_line: Harden doesn't have much experience in the slot, but a nickel role would emphasize his strengths — quickness, run support and competitiveness — and mitigate his NFL concerns — long speed and length. He could be a starting nickel at some point.

profile: Hardy plays with a lot of confidence despite his size. He'll be an outlier in that regard, but that smaller size allows him to flip his hips quickly to adjust to two-way route options when defending the slot. It also empowers him to squeeze between small rush lanes on the blitz. He lacks strength, as one would expect. But when it comes to making contact at the catch point, he is still disruptive enough to cause some drops. There is some concern about his long speed, which is why the team that drafts him won't want him in press coverage, especially on the outside. He does much better with off- coverage spacing in zone.
strengths: Understands how to stay between his man and the ball Good eyes in off-coverage Quick player on the blitz who can fit through small rush lanes Smaller size allows him to flip his hips very quickly, which is important for defending receivers in space
weaknesses: Limited long speed Quickness is average at best Won't match up well against bigger slot receivers due to small size
bottom_line: Hardy is a smaller slot cornerback who plays with a lot of confidence despite his lack of size. He is quick but likely lacks the top-gear speed necessary for successful secondary play at the next level.

profile: Despite injuries, Hart managed to start 32 games at outside cornerback over the past three seasons. He is a physical zone cornerback who is very competitive, showing a willingness and good fundamentals in the run game. His overall athleticism is concerning, though. Too often receivers were able to get even and separate against him when running vertical routes. His acceleration speed is decent, but it is more build-up speed than twitchiness. Overall, Hart has ideal length and experience to be a mid-round off-coverage cornerback in a zone-heavy system. The NFL team that drafts him won't want to use him in press coverage much.
strengths: Fantastic length and size to hold up against press coverage and affect the catch point Brings a willingness to support in run defense Competitive player Good feel for spacing in off-coverage from zone
weaknesses: Long speed is a concern, which makes a press coverage projection tricky. When receivers get even with him, they create separation Acceleration is more build-up than it is twitchy. Impacts recovery speed Start-and-stop ability is just OK, given his size
bottom_line: Hart brings ideal size to the outside cornerback spot. There are some natrural movement concerns that come with a bigger body, but when he anticipates, he can play at a reliable level as a rotational cornerback.

profile: Jackson's skill set is that of a press-man cornerback. He is tall and long but also a fluid and explosive athlete — a rare combination. His recovery speed, hip flexibility and footwork are much better than most players with his measurables. He consistently gets his head around to look to bat down or intercept passes. His slender build can hinder him in press coverage and when he is finishing tackles, but his missed tackle rate is quite low and his run-defense grade in 2023 was reliable. The biggest negative in Jackson’s game is his anticipation. Too often the better receivers he faced made cuts that he did not anticipate well enough to mirror.
strengths: Physical player who likes to get hands on receivers early in press and then hand fight through the route Length is a huge plus for press and also for forced incompletions Impressive mirror ability for a player with such long legs Consistently gets his head around to face the passer to try to break up or intercept passes Did not miss many tackles in 2023 on his way to a high run-D grade
weaknesses: Though he fares well in press, he can get pushed off balance against stronger receivers Has good recovery speed but needs to anticipate better so he isn't as behind when players get vertical
bottom_line: Jackson is an alluring prospect because his size and athletic combination doesn't come around often. However, he must anticipate routes better and not rely on his recovery speed as much. If he can do this, he can be a starting-caliber cornerback in the NFL with a shutdown skill set.

profile: James is a competitive cornerback who has experience in man and zone, as well as in press and off coverages. He's on the smaller side in weight and length, and that shows up at the catch point and when taking on blocks. With his smaller size, though, he possesses well above-average quickness and acceleration. He has the fluid hips to mirror and match off the line in press. Although he is quick, his long speed is average at best, which might hold him back from being a starter at the next level.
strengths: Spry movement skills at his lower weight profile One of the few players who handled Malik Nabers' quickness Is a fiery competitor who loves man coverage Explosive in short areas and can flip his hips and accelerate quickly Visible pre- and post-snap communicator
weaknesses: Lower weight profile shows up as a deficiency when taking on blocks and when tackling Though he is feisty, he gets pushed back and walled off decently easily versus blockers Lacks great top speed for in trail technique
bottom_line: James brings the competitiveness and mentality you want from a cornerback. His lack of top speed and strength likely limit him to a rotational or spot starter role.

profile: Most of Jones' work came as an outside CB with a good amount of assignment slot coverage too. He has good height and length for press coverage, which is where he is most comfortable. When he can get hands on receivers early, he can stay on their hip (former track star athleticism shows up there). He also has a good feel for when the ball is arriving for PBUs. He gets in trouble when he's in off coverage, as he is not comfortable in space and lacks the patience and overall discipline to not get put in trail when not in press. His lower weight makes it tougher for him to make tackles (ankle tackler), though he is willing.
strengths: Vast experience has given him a quick sense for reactions pre-snap. Competitive play who is constantly looking to make the big play (and celebrate afterward). Has man coverage experience outside and in the slot. Comfortable and confident when he can get hands on receivers. Instinctive ball skills for when to turn and look and when to swipe.
weaknesses: Feels out of control too often, especially when asked to play off coverage. Lower weight makes him an ankle tackler. Overaggressive at times. Combine athletic scores were good, but he gets beat in space and is in trail too much with not enough recovery speed to consistently make up for it on tape.
bottom_line: Jones has the length and movement skills to find a role as a backup outside corner for a team that likes to play a lot of press-man coverage.

profile: Jones transferred to Florida State after one year at Mississippi State, and he blossomed into an impact player. He was primarily an outside cornerback through the first four years of his college career, but his below-average long speed/recovery speed was exposed there, especially when asked to play press. In 2023, he played in the slot and had a career year. He has the traits to succeed as a slot defender at the next level, boasting quick feet, hips and acceleration to stick with players in space. He also brings great awareness of spacing and throwing paths, and he is consistently conscious of putting himself between the receiver and the ball.
strengths: Quick and balanced footwork in his backpedal Quickness is a calling card of his game. It shows in his hips and acceleration Willing run defender. Even executed some rip moves to get around blockers in run defense Reliable tackler Smart from the slot. When in trail technique, knows to take the path that naturally cuts off passes, specifically on deep crossers
weaknesses: Limited long speed. Likely why he was pushed into the slot
bottom_line: It took a while for Jones to find a home at slot cornerback, but since doing so, he has shown valuable skills that should translate to the NFL. His quickness, both physically and mentally, projects well to the slot as a rotational defensive back or nickel starter.

profile: King started nine games as a true sophomore with the Nittany Lions and was one of the best cornerbacks in the country, posting an elite single-coverage grade. The 2023 campaign was a different story, but he still brings athleticism and smooth movement with explosiveness. His feet are fast but often look on the verge of being out of control. Though his click-and-close ability is above average, he does not anticipate route breaks quickly enough to make an impact or warrant no-throws as much as he should. King is a willing run defender, but his pursuit angles and technique are unreliable, which makes it unlikely he will ever feature in the slot.
strengths: Displayed such good athleticism in 2022 that he didn't even need to get hands on receivers to mirror them in press Rare combination of explosive yet smooth, even in his backpedals Willing run defender, though not a strong or consistent one
weaknesses: Bad pursuit angles in run defense. Tends to be overaggressive Not a fundamentally sound tackler, even when diving for ankles Anticipation could be better, especially for in-breaking routes. Has the athleticism to make more plays Footwork is fast but can look nearly out of control Shorter arms impact how well he can get his hands to the ball at the catch point
bottom_line: Although King has a lot of athletic potential at outside cornerback, his anticipation, instincts and technique are too inconsistent. He projects as a mid-round prospect who needs time to develop, but he offers a starting-caliber payoff if he improves.

profile: Lassiter is a very smart football player, especially for his age and experience. He understands that winning at cornerback starts with anticipation, controlled footwork and fundamentally sound hand placement and hand fighting. He is somewhat limited when it comes to twitchiness. He is controlled and can change direction quickly, but his first step doesn't explode as well as it does for other cornerbacks, and his long speed, while adequate, needs more build-up. In run defense, he is conscious of funneling players inward but does so too conservatively, at times, and then fails to make a good tackle attempt.
strengths: From his hands to his feet, Lassiter is a smart, fundamentally sound player who understands the importance of technique Hand placement and punch timing in press are reliable and consistent Not the fastest footwork, but he looks in control at all times Savvy hand fighter throughout the route Smart and sound run defender who does not give up the sideline and funnels ball carriers in
weaknesses: A good but not great athlete when it comes to recovery speed and burst Long speed can be adequate, but it needs build-up time Sometimes too conservative with funneling players in run D Not much ball production despite playing more than 1,500 snaps the past two years
bottom_line: Lassiter is a competitive, scheme-versatile cornerback who can succeed in both man and zone assignments. While he isn't the best athlete at the position, he makes up for it in many ways, including through instincts and anticipation. He projects as a priority Day 2 selection as a future CB2.

profile: McGlothern might have the height to suggest he'd be a press- man corner, but his best plays come when he can adjust off the line of scrimmage in Cover 3 or quarters coverage. His natural instincts can shine, enabling him to undercut routes for PBUs and INTs. When it comes to tackling, he is wildly inconsistent right now. There are times when effort is lacking, and other times when his fundamentals are. It's hard to rely on him in run support. Back in coverage, he displays the athletic ability to stop, turn and close the gap on comeback routes, but there are also too many times when he just feels out of control.
strengths: Twenty-one forced incompletions and seven interceptions over the last two seasons. Natural feel for coverage — a lot of his best plays are when he can keep his eyes on the ball and make a break. Displays the ability to stop, turn and run to close the gap and make a play on comeback routes.
weaknesses: He is not interested in doing the dirty work for run defense on the edge. Tackling technique is quite inconsistent. Feels out of control too often — hard to know what you'll get on a play-by-play basis.
bottom_line: McGlothern has some fantastic ball production thanks to top- tier instincts in off-coverage, but his freelancing is a gift and a curse. He's a true boom-or-bust player, not just for his career but on a play-by-play basis.

profile: How smart and talented is McKinstry? He started as a true freshman in a Nick Saban defense. At 6-foot-1, he has good size and length to match up on the outside against bigger receivers. He is very comfortable and experienced in press- man coverage and also has a good feel for spacing in zone. He has an uncanny knack for making plays on the ball despite being in trail technique and not having his eyes toward the pocket. McKinstry's best attribute is his demeanor. He never seems panicked — in any facet of play. He is a good athlete but not an elite one for the NFL level when it comes to stop- and-start ability. He is not as twitchy as he is smooth.
strengths: Great balance and fluidity when backpedaling Good, but not great, recovery speed Length is a big plus for press coverage Hands are quick and precise for disrupting receivers out of press Nice shoulder dip reaction time to avoid blocks Comfortable and confident in "island" coverage Does not fall for feet chopping of WRs in their releases. Quick to read screens
weaknesses: Change-of-direction ability and agility are good but not elite for stickiness in coverage when routes are breaking Likes to be physical, which led to some unnecessary holding and DPI penalties Long speed is good but not elite Could stand to be more aggressive when attacking the ball
bottom_line: McKinstry plays one of the most difficult positions in the game with so much poise and production. He might not be an elite athlete, but he is one of the smartest cornerback prospects you'll find. He can play in any defensive scheme and is the type of player you draft in the first round.

profile: Melton’s brother Bo currently plays wide receiver for the Green Bay Packers. Max has been starting since his true freshman season at outside cornerback, but his lack of size and long speed suggests a switch to the slot could be in his NFL future. He has quick and controlled footwork when changing directions, though he isn't as sticky in coverage as one would want for a slot cornerback. That could be more anticipation-related than athletic. He does his best work in off-coverage, where his downhill speed and anticipation shine brightest. He is a willing defender in run support, though he missed many tackles in 2023.
strengths: Strong awareness and anticipation in off-coverage Fluid hips to change direction Quick, controlled footwork which leads to solid stop-and-start ability in space Recovery speed is adequate when he is coming downhill
weaknesses: Does not seem as fast when running with outside receivers vertically as he does when triggering downhill Experienced in press but better when he can play off-coverage, specifically as an outside CB Not as sticky in coverage when it comes to quick movement in space. Feels like an anticipation thing more than a knock on his athletic ability
bottom_line: Melton is an intriguing cornerback prospect because the slot might be his best role in the NFL. He does bring a lot of experience on the outside, though. Melton projects as a priority Day 3 pick with inside-outside versatility.

profile: No FBS cornerback forced more incompletions over the past two seasons than Mitchell. He did so while playing an off- coverage role in a Cover 3-heavy scheme. He would align himself 8-10 yards off the line of scrimmage, keep his eyes on the quarterback and wait to pounce. His recovery speed and acceleration are both elite, even for NFL standards. He does not have much experience in press, but he has the size and movement skills to succeed there. His instincts in zone are still a work in progress. He didn’t miss many tackles in run defense, but his technique isn't as fundamentally sound as it could be.
strengths: Very impressive athlete. Body control, explosiveness and top speed are all well above average for the pros Backpedal is smooth and loaded to break on the ball at any sec Downhill speed in off-coverage is strong. Quarterbacks threw his way a lot because they didn't believe he could get there, and yet, he often did Anticipation in off-coverage is excellent.
weaknesses: Still working on his feel/instincts in zone coverage. Can lose guys when they're in his zone but he's not looking right at them Can be overaggressive against double moves Strike timing in press is inconsistent due to a lack of experience
bottom_line: Mitchell recorded some of the best advanced coverage metrics over a two-year sample size in the PFF college era. He has all the ability in the world to be a CB1 at the next level, but his lack of experience in press coverage could stop him from being a unanimous first-round pick on every team's board.

profile: Newton was a two-star wide receiver recruit before making the switch to cornerback when he enrolled at Louisiana- Monroe. He spent three seasons there before transferring to TCU. He brings a ton of experience, starting 58 games in college while playing more than 1,700 snaps over the past two years alone. In 2022, he showed a lot of confidence and quickness, leading to plenty of forced incompletions and interceptions. But he was not the same player in 2023. His anticipation of routes, releases and breaks was a step behind. While he is quick, his long speed proved to be an issue against NFL-caliber receivers.
strengths: Very fast footwork. Smooth when transitioning from backpedal into his strides Hips flip quickly, which helps when in press to be able to adjust in either direction Calm and confident in trail technique
weaknesses: Doesn't sink super low in his backpedal and can look off-balance Anticipation got worse in 2023 Long-speed issues showed up in 2023, especially against Texas
bottom_line: Newton's 2022 tape was much better than his 2023 film as primarily a press-man coverage defender. Depending on which teams believe in more, he could be drafted anywhere from the second round to the fifth round.

profile: Phillips did not gain much starting experience from his four years at Kentucky. He played in every game in 2022 but was a rotational player in the slot and on the outside. In 2023, he was a consistent starter at outside cornerback. He brings a physical brand of play to the position, and that lends itself well to press coverage, where he is most confident. He is a strong run defender from the slot and can set the edge, stop screens and make tackles. Phillips’ deficiencies are on display in play off-coverage. His lack of starting experience shows in his spacing and timing for contact. He also must improve the fluidity and precision in his hip turns.
strengths: Impressive run defender from the slot. Has the mentality, fundamentals and strength to set the edge, blitz effectively and collapse Plays a physical brand of coverage. Works well from press Seems more confident in his movement skills in press
weaknesses: Relies on the speed turn too much. Yields separation when the receiver breaks from his leverage Hip flips aren't as smooth as they need to be for off-coverage Is not as confident in zone coverage. Spacing is off and contact is mistimed
bottom_line: Phillips' physical profile makes him an interesting cornerback to develop in the Day 3 range for a team that likes to play heavy press coverage.

profile: Pritchett proved quite versatile at Auburn, playing mostly outside cornerback but also seeing some snaps in the slot and as a punt and kick returner. His first-step acceleration and hip fluidity are above average for a player of his size. His long speed is decent, but when he faces quicker, faster receivers, he gets too grabby. He is more effective in off- coverage. His lower weight profile shows up when tackling. He dives at ankles too often, and when he does tackle with sound technique, he lacks the density and strength to truly stop ball carriers. He uses his long arms to force incompletions, but he lacks natural takeaway abilities.
strengths: Has nice first-step acceleration, allowing him to close downhill quickly Hips are decently fluid for a player over 6-foot
weaknesses: Ankle-diver when tackling Does not have the strength/density for physicality in the run game in the NFL Balance in his backpedal can be an issue out of press. Weight is too far back Needs to grab to keep up with quicker receivers
bottom_line: Pritchett's quickness and special teams experience make him a cornerback to draft and develop. But unless he gets stronger, it will be tough to keep him on the field in a full-time role in the NFL.

profile: Rakestraw is an incredibly smart and savvy off-coverage cornerback who plays in a way that makes watching his film a joy. Before the ball is even snapped, you can see evidence of his football IQ in his pre-snap communication and adjustments to motion. He does most of his work in off- coverage (Cover 3, quarters and underneath zones), but does so beautifully, showing excellent spacing and an ability to pass off routes with ease. He is not asked to play press or single coverage often, which makes his true mirror/recovery speed a question. But his fluid hips, quick feet, good burst and excellent instincts are starting-caliber traits.
strengths: Excellent eyes and instincts in zone coverage. Consistent pre-snap communicator Patient player who is in control at all times. No panic in him Quick feet for change of direction Smooth hips when changing direction Not a strong run defender, but still likes to be physical Reliable when funneling ball carriers to sideline and back inside Experienced and comfortable in the slot
weaknesses: True recovery speed/straight-line speed are worries. Might be why he's primarily a zone cornerback, but seems adequate enough Lack of ball production in his final year
bottom_line: Rakestraw possesses a high football IQ and does great work in off-coverage when he can anticipate with space. He is a quick and controlled cornerback who will provide plus reliability as a run defender. His traits are worthy of a top-50 draft pick, but his lack of ball production might have him drafted just outside that range.

profile: Richardson possesses ideal size, speed and length combination for the NFL level, especially when he can play closer to the line of scrimmage. Such an alignment also allows one of his biggest strengths to shine: His willingness and reliability in run support. When in coverage, Richardson's biggest weakness is his lack of feel and anticipation. He isn't as comfortable and confident as required when playing certain leverage, and he does not have a good feel for when the ball is arriving, hence the lack of ball production over the years (no interceptions in his career).
strengths: Willing to come up in run support despite lower weight. Strong tackler when he gets his hands on ball carriers. Good size, speed and length combination to be sticky in coverage.
weaknesses: Naturally upright position makes it tougher for him to really flip the hips and change direction with balance and explosiveness. Needs to improve anticipation so he can play more in control. Doesn't have a ton of confidence in how to play leverages correctly — can get turned around too much. Did not record an interception in his college career (only 10 forced incompletions in four years as well).
bottom_line: Richardson is a good athlete to bet on early day three with plus run support skills, but he has to anticipate better to remain in control down the field and to get his hands on the football every now and then.

profile: Sainristil played receiver in his first three years at Michigan before moving to defensive back full time in 2022. He has excellent body control and athletic ability for the position. His feet are quick, controlled and loaded to break on the ball right when he needs to. His long speed isn't elite, but it is adequate. His wide receiver skill set has translated to cornerback in the form of top-tier ball skills. On top of all that, he is fearlessly physical at the catch point, when attacking blocks and when tackling. Though he tends to go for ankle tackles regularly due to his smaller size, he doesn't shy away from physicality.
strengths: Impressive reaction speed Well-above-average click-and-close ability Fearless physical player in run defense and when taking on blocks Smart zone player. Doesn't just drop to a spot. Footwork is quick, controlled, balanced and loaded to accelerate and break on the ball Consistently disruptive/physical at the catch point Fiery competitor
weaknesses: Lacking in long speed. Ohio State’s Emeka Egbuka exposed that in 2022 Can be too aggressive to make plays in run defense and loses contain to the sideline
bottom_line: Every NFL team would love to have a player like Sainristil. He brings a great skill set and mentality to be a starting slot cornerback, with safety and special teams versatility to boot. He should be viewed as one of the top "football players" in this draft, regardless of position.

profile: Smith was a three-star recruit out of high school but very quickly outplayed that rating. He is a bigger slot player, which comes with useful extra power. He played the STAR position, a hybrid between a slot defender and linebacker, in Georgia’s system. In that role, he showcased his strength of taking on tight ends and offensive tackles better than most defensive backs. He is limited athletically, with adequate first-step explosiveness to change direction but below-average recovery speed and long speed. He is an aggressive tackler who sometimes takes poor pursuit angles. He also has ample experience and success as a gunner on punt and kick teams.
strengths: Powerful and bigger than most slot CBs. Comes with plus ability to take on blocks and play near the box Good tackler with some hit power for forcing fumbles Can set the edge well against tight ends Good first-step explosiveness
weaknesses: Limited in his top speed/cover speed. Was replaced by Kamari Lassiter against Missouri for the Luther Burden III matchup Takes some overaggressive pursuit angles that he doesn't have the speed for
bottom_line: NFL teams that like to stack the box and be more aggressive on the line of scrimmage will be drawn to Smith’s power when setting the edge in run defense. Ultimately, his lack of long speed could cause him to have issues in coverage.

profile: Smith-Wade's coaches have raved about his maturity levels now compared to when he was coming out of high school, and his development as a player correlates with his off-field growth. Smith-Wade is small, even for a smaller position, but he doesn't let that hold him back from going all out in the physical parts of the game, tackling and press coverage. His size would make outside coverage tough, but his short-area movement skills hint at potential starting ability as a slot cornerback in the NFL.
strengths: Does not let his lack of size affect how hard he plays. Short-area movement skills are ideal for slot coverage. Feet are lightning quick.
weaknesses: Lack of weight may not affect his mentality, but it does allow receivers to push him around. Doesn't bring a powerful presence for tackles. Often dives at ankles.
bottom_line: Smith-Wade is the manifestation of the phrase "It's not the size of the dog in the fight, but the size of the fight in the dog." His lack of NFL measurables limits his potential as an outside cornerback, but his short-area movement skills could yield a starting role in the slot.

profile: It's impressive to watch a cornerback of Tampa's size move the way he does. His start-and-stop ability for a player who has more mass and longer legs is well above average. As one would expect, his long arms are excellent for ball production. He ranked in the 98th percentile for forced incompletion rate on passes thrown his way in college. He is physical in coverage but still dives at ankles for tackles quite a bit. His footwork is good in his initial backpedal, but he can get turned around and lose his leverage, at times, leading to separation. If Tampa can clean that up, he can be a very sticky cornerback.
strengths: Impressive foot speed and fluidity for as tall as he is Long legs and strides typically make it tough for defensive backs to change direction and close, but not for Tampa Long arms are very advantageous for forced incompletions Physical when getting off block. Long arms help there, too Is eager to get his head around to make a play on the ball Is as confident in the slot as he is on the outside Loves the bump-and-run style of coverage
weaknesses: Not as much experience in press man as you would think when looking at his measurables Physical as a tackler, but does dive at ankles quite a bit Long speed is an issue, at times, but it's plenty adequate and not as bad as you might expect for a player his size Can get turned around by more agile receivers
bottom_line: Tampa's unique fluidity and size for a cornerback make him worthy of a top-75 pick. If he can clean up his footwork, he can be a starting outside cornerback in the NFL with the potential to be an impact player.

profile: Wiggins' 6-foot-2 frame and length allow him to disrupt receivers in the contact window and at the catch point. He also has above-average athleticism for the position. His footwork is quick and controlled, his hips flip fluidly and fast and he has impressive recovery speed. Although Wiggins didn’t have many interceptions, his forced incompletion percentage and awareness prove that he is impactful. The best part about him is he remains confident in both man and zone responsibilities. He has a slender build, and that shows up when tasked with tackling, getting off blocks and handling stronger receivers in their routes.
strengths: Rare athleticism. Smooth yet explosive Elite recovery speed Really good arm length to hand fight in press and disrupt the catch point Very quick and fluid hips Feet are light, quick and balanced Equally as confident in man or zone Competitive player who does not back down
weaknesses: Slender build. Shows up in run defense, though he did improve there in 2023 Lack of weight allows offensive players to push him around, especially in the run game
bottom_line: Wiggins has the tools of a first-round, high-impact cornerback. His athleticism will never be in question, nor will his competitiveness. Those two characteristics should yield a long- term starting player.

profile: Despite playing only three years of college ball, Bishop has 35 games and 29 starts under his belt. He is a box/slot- safety type of player who does his best work coming downhill. His feet are constantly moving and light, which allows him to break on the ball or a receiver at any moment. He is often square with his form when approaching ball carriers and can wrap up. His slot coverage grade hasn't been great over the last few years, but he is versatile enough to play there. He does not have a good feel for single-high responsibilities, and his overall feel for space in zone coverage is still a work in progress.
strengths: Feet are constantly moving. He's always at the ready to break on the ball or a receiver Reliable tackler who will rally to the ball but not get overaggressive Pretty good block shedding for a defensive back. He is a strong wrap-up tackler Slot coverage grade isn't great, but he is versatile enough to play there vs. certain receivers
weaknesses: Not a single-high-safety type of player, which is fine Lack of length does show up when wrapping up tackles and also in getting off blocks Still working on the feel for zone coverage Gets trigger-happy coming downhill. It leaves him open for double moves, pump fakes and over pursuit.
bottom_line: Bishop has starting potential as a strong safety and slot defender, but his overaggressive tendencies and lack of patience in zone will require more discipline at the NFL level.

profile: Brade is a physical safety who is a willing and effective tackler against even the biggest ball carriers. He played more than 1,500 snaps over the last two seasons alone at a near- even split between free safety and strong safety. He is most confident when kept in a downhill role closer to the linebacker level. When he has to play deep coverage, he does not look as comfortable and can lose receivers passing through his zone. He is a decent athlete overall, but his change of direction and acceleration appear below average for the position.
strengths: Willing tackler with good size to bring down bigger ball carriers/tight ends Confident player when he can keep his eyes and momentum downhill
weaknesses: Overall athleticism is middling Recovery speed is average at best Heavy feet for a DB Can get turned around/lost in deep coverage
bottom_line: Brade comes with good size and a willingness to tackle as an experienced defensive back. However, a lack of NFL-level athleticism will likely limit him to a rotational role as a box safety.

profile: Bullock has top-tier range and does his best work from a single-high alignment. He has the long speed, hip fluidity and footwork to break on the ball and cover a ton of ground. He is also good at reading and baiting quarterbacks into throws. He shows off wide receiver-like ball skills when defending the pass. Most of the negatives on his scouting report are in run defense. He is slender and currently lacks NFL-level strength/density to be reliable there. Though his movement skills are cornerback-like and can translate to slot coverage, his strength is an issue when playing near the line of scrimmage or against tight ends in man coverage.
strengths: Elite movement skills/range Hips/feet are like a cornerback Wide receiver-like ball skills Good ability to watch a QB’s eyes and bait them into throws
weaknesses: Lacks NFL-level strength/density when tackling Struggles to match up with tight ends due to lack of strength Can get lost in his gap fits Lack of strength causes him to get reckless when tackling
bottom_line: Bullock's lack of strength will limit how much an NFL team can trust him to play early in his career. But if he can get stronger, he possesses elite range as an impactful single-high safety for any defense, especially in Cover 3 and Cover 1.

profile: Hicks played in just one game as a true freshman at Washington State, enduring some early struggles that lit a fire under him. As a redshirt freshman, he started 11 of 13 games, and he was once again a full-time starter in 2023. He is a consistent pre-snap communicator when the offense uses motion and does well to anticipate where the ball is going in zone/roaming coverage roles. Hicks demonstrates tone-setting tackling. His cornerback background gives him a good baseline for slot man coverage assignments. He still lacks long speed and twitch, but when he can keep things in front of him, he has good speed to make plays downhill.
strengths: Solid tackler Consistent pre-snap communication Adequate linear athlete in split-safety roles Viable slot player, especially against tight ends Good eyes for robber coverage roles Comfortable and capable when playing at the linebacker level
